changed.from: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), the canonical contrast dimension is \(d=0\), so \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)\) for all units and \(\theta(t)=s_1(t)\). Along every regular submodel that perturbs \(\theta\) through the post-control law, the score contribution of the target-pre records is identically zero. Thus target-pre data are \(\theta\)-ancillary at exact rank one, while the canonical target-loading derivative is nonzero on a normalization-preserving submodel of \(\mathfrak P_r\) for every fixed \(r\ge2\).
changed.to: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), the canonical contrast dimension is \(d=0\), so \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)\) for every unit and \(\theta(t)=s_1(t)\). Along every regular submodel whose target-pre marginal law is fixed and which perturbs \(\theta\) through the post-control law, the score contribution of the target-pre records is identically zero. For fixed \(r\ge2\), any normalization-preserving loading path \(z_{\star,\eta}=z_\star+\eta v\) that remains in \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) has target derivative \(\left.\partial_\eta\theta_\eta(t)\right|_{\eta=0}=b_1(t)^\top v\), which is nonzero exactly when \(b_1^\top v\not\equiv0\) on \(\mathcal I\).
changed.reason: The original score assertion omitted the necessary fixed-target-pre-marginal qualification, and its final existence clause was stronger than the derivative identity supplied by the rank assumptions.

changed.from: There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{int}}<\infty\) such that, for the interpolation rule in \(\mathrm{def:inference-grid}\), the difference between the continuous-time supremum error and its grid supremum is at most \(c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^\beta\) uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_r\). Consequently the explicit interpolation allowance is \(O(\rho_r)\) and continuous-time honesty is not obtained by silently replacing \(\mathcal I\) with a fixed finite grid.
changed.to:
There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)<\infty\) such that, for the piecewise-linear interpolant \(\widehat\theta_r\) in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr-multiplier-band}\),
\[
 0\le \|\widehat\theta_r-\theta\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}
 -\max_{g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}}|\widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)|
 \le c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\). Consequently the interpolation allowance under the corrected grid definition is \(O(\rho_r)\), so continuous-time honesty is not obtained by replacing \(\mathcal I\) with a fixed finite grid.
changed.reason: A \(C^\beta\) hazard gives a \(C^{\beta+1}\) survival curve, while piecewise-linear interpolation saturates at second order; for \(\beta>2\), the frozen \(h^\beta\) claim is false.

changed.from: Choose a deterministic grid \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\) containing zero and \(\bar\tau\) whose mesh obeys \(h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^\beta\le\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), and use piecewise-linear interpolation between adjacent grid points.
changed.to: Choose a deterministic grid \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\) containing \(0\) and \(\bar\tau\) whose mesh satisfies \(h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}\le\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), and use piecewise-linear interpolation between adjacent grid points.
changed.reason: The mesh must be matched to the actual piecewise-linear interpolation exponent \(\min\{\beta+1,2\}\).

changed.from: Compute every \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\). Center the donor curves, retain the first \(d=r-1\) functional principal contrasts, estimate \(z_\star\) by minimum-norm least squares from \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}-\widehat s_0\), and set \(\widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star\), with \(\widehat\theta_1=\widehat s_1\). Linearize this map jointly in all cellwise Kaplan--Meier counting-process martingales. Replace each patient martingale increment by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times its estimated increment, recompute the linearized target process, and take its conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile in grid supremum norm. Define \(\widehat B_r\) by adding and subtracting that quantile and the deterministic interpolation allowance \(Lh_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^\beta\), interpolate linearly, clip to \([0,1]\), and impose the common endpoint value one at time zero.
changed.to:
On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by linear interpolation.  For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices.  If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define the measurable positive-part scales \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\).  Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\).  Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\).  On the regular event that both folds are nonempty, \(\widehat\lambda_d>0\), \(\widehat\lambda_d>\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\), and \(\widehat H_0\) is positive definite, define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
The fitted curve is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace.  If a fold is empty, a selected eigenvalue is nonpositive, there is a cutoff tie, or \(\widehat H_0\) is singular, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve.  Thus \((\widehat s_p,\widehat b_p,\widehat z_\star,\widehat\theta_r)\) is a measurable function of every dataset.

On the regular event, differentiate the rotation-invariant composite map, including the spectral projector and positive square-root scales, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment.  On the fallback event, define the empirical derivative to be the ordinary pooled Kaplan--Meier derivative.  Replace each patient contribution by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times that contribution, and let \(c_r^\xi\) be the conditional \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\)-quantile of its grid supremum, where
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}{2}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widetilde\theta_r\) be the pointwise projection of \(\widehat\theta_r\) onto \([0,1]\), with value one imposed at zero.  With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)\) from the interpolation proposition, define the grid endpoints by
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(g)=\max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r(g)-c_r^\xi-c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+c_r^\xi+c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\}.
\]
Interpolate both endpoints linearly and impose the common value one at zero.  This total measurable construction defines \(\widehat B_r\) and its multiplier process for every dataset.
changed.reason: The raw same-sample covariance has errors-in-variables attenuation and the frozen algorithm is undefined at negative cross-fold eigenvalues, cutoff ties, and singular loading regressions.  The corrected construction cross-fits, uses measurable positive-part scaling, and specifies a total fallback and multiplier rule.

changed.from: Set \(x_m=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}/\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}\), so \(N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}x_m=0\), \(N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}x_m^2=1\), and \(\max_m|x_m|<\sqrt 3\). Choose the declared fixed constants \(a_{\circ,0},a_{\circ,1},\lambda_\circ,h_\circ\) in the interior of the class bounds, with \(h_\circ\) small enough for the displayed density floor. For \(u\in\{-1,+1\}\), put \(s_p(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}\), \(b_p(t)=a_{\circ,p}\psi_\circ(t)\), \(z_m=x_m\) for donors, and \(z_\star^{(u)}=u h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}\). Define \(S_{p,m}^{(u)}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)z_m\) on \(\mathcal I\), continue it after \(\bar\tau\) by \(S_{p,m}^{(u)}(\bar\tau)e^{-\lambda_\circ(t-\bar\tau)}\), and take \(C_{p,m,j}=\infty\). The constants are chosen so the densities \(f_{p,m}^{(u)}=-\partial_tS_{p,m}^{(u)}\) obey \(f_{p,m}^{(u)}\ge c_f\) on the support of \(\psi_\circ'\). The resulting observed-data laws are \(P_u\).
changed.to:
Fix \(d=r-1\).  For every integer \(N_0\ge2d+1\) and \(1\le k\le d\), define the explicitly centered donor column
\[
 q_{k,m}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}^k-
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N_0}\{\ell-(N_0+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le m\le N_0.
\]
Apply deterministic empirical Gram--Schmidt to \(q_1,\ldots,q_d\) in the inner product \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m xy\), orienting each column to have positive leading polynomial coefficient, and denote the resulting row vectors by \(z_m^{(N_0,d)}\).  Thus every column is mean zero and \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m z_m^{(N_0,d)}z_m^{(N_0,d)\top}=I_d\); for \(d=1\), \(z_{m,1}^{(N_0,1)}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}/\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}\).

For \(d\ge1\), apply deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\) Gram--Schmidt to \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), orient the first function as \(\varphi_{1,d}=\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), write \(\Phi_d=(\varphi_{1,d},\ldots,\varphi_{d,d})^\top\), and set
\[
 A_{p,d}(t)=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d(t).
\]
For \(u\in\{-1,+1\}\), take \(s_p(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}\), \(b_p=A_{p,d}\), donor loadings \(z_m=z_m^{(N_0,d)}\), and target loading \(z_\star^{(u)}=u h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}e_1\).  Put
\[
 S_{p,m}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 S_{p,\star}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_\star^{(u)}
\]
on \(\mathcal I\), continue every curve after \(\bar\tau\) by its value at \(\bar\tau\) times \(e^{-\lambda_\circ(t-\bar\tau)}\), take \(C_{p,m,j}=\infty\), and let \(P_{r,u}\) be the induced independent observed-data law.  For \(r=2\), define \(P_u=P_{2,u}\).  When \(d=0\), all score arrays and factor terms are empty and the same prescription defines the homogeneous backbone.  This construction only names the laws; centering, empirical Gram, class membership, rank, spectrum, separation, and divergence are properties to be proved.
changed.reason: The converse needs a total fixed-rank embedding.  Every polynomial score is now centered before empirical Gram--Schmidt, and the orthogonal factor backbone and laws \(P_{r,+}\) and \(P_{r,-}\) are explicit rather than hidden in a membership assertion.

changed.to:
Put \(d=r-1\).  For \(d\ge1\), let \(z_m^{(N,d)}\) be obtained, for each \(N\ge2d+1\), by empirical Gram--Schmidt from the explicitly centered columns
\[
 q_{k,m}^{(N)}=\{m-(N+1)/2\}^k-N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\{\ell-(N+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le k\le d,
\]
and define \(R_d=\sup_{N\ge2d+1}\max_{1\le m\le N}\|z_m^{(N,d)}\|_2\), with \(R_0=0\).  Let \(\Phi_d\) be the deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\)-orthonormalization of \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), with first coordinate \(\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), and put \(A_{p,d}=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d\).  The fixed primitive constants obey
\[
 g_-\le1,
 \qquad
 R_d\le M_z,
 \qquad
 \gamma_-^2\le(a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2)\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\gamma_+^2,
 \qquad
 \kappa_-\le a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\kappa_+,
\]
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}\|A_{p,d}(t)\|_2\le M_b,
 \qquad
 2|a_{\circ,0}|h_\circ c_f^{-1/2}
 \left\{\int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac34(1/2-\alpha).
\]
Writing \(v_\circ=|a_{\circ,1}|/4\), for every \(p\in\{0,1\}\), every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) with \(\|x\|_2\le R_d\), every \(|v|\le v_\circ\), and every \(t\in\mathcal I\), the curve
\[
 \ell_{p,x,v}(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}+A_{p,d}(t)^\top x+\mathbf 1\{p=1\}v\psi_\circ(t)
\]
satisfies
\[
 s_-\le\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\le1,
 \qquad
 -\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{t\in\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')}[-\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)]\ge c_f,
 \qquad
 \left\|-\frac{\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}}{\ell_{p,x,v}}\right\|_{C^\beta(\mathcal I)}\le L.
\]
For \(d=0\), the same four inequalities hold with the empty factor term, \(x=0\), and every \(|v|\le v_\circ\).

\[

 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.

\[

 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+c_r^\xi+c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\}.
\]

changed.from: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and all sequences with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\to\infty\), the functional-PCR estimator has an expansion in \(\ell^\infty(\mathcal I)\), \[\widehat\theta_r-\theta=\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}K_T^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_T}\phi_{T,j}+(N_0K_D)^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\phi_{D,p,m,j}+R_r,\qquad \|R_r\|_\infty=o_P(\rho_r),\] where the displayed sums are independent mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes, the target process \(\phi_{T,j}\) is identically zero when \(r=1\), and the patient-multiplier analogue consistently estimates the law of the normalized supremum without a restriction on the relative growth of \(K_T\) and \(N_0K_D\).
changed.to:
Put \(n_D=N_0K_D\), let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and center the functional-PCR map at the interpolated population panel \(\widetilde S^0=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and all sequences with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\to\infty\), there are independent mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes \(\phi_{T,j}\) and \(\phi_{D,p,m,j}\), a deterministic grid function \(\mathfrak b_r\), and a remainder \(Q_r\) such that, simultaneously for \(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)=Z_r(g)+\mathfrak b_r(g)+Q_r(g),
 \qquad
 Z_r=\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}K_T^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_T}\phi_{T,j}
     +n_D^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\phi_{D,p,m,j},
\]
where \(\phi_{T,j}\equiv0\) when \(r=1\) and
\[
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}
 \le \mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D).
\]
The interpolated population comparison equals \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\theta\), and hence equals \(\theta\) at every grid point. For every sufficiently large evaluated triple, the finite-tail buffer and the conditional multiplier critical value in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\) obey
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}P\{\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>\omega_r/2\}
 \le\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)/4,
\]
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}P\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>c_r^\xi+\omega_r/2\}
 \le\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)/4.
\]

For an observed control cell with \(k\) patients and \(k\) large enough, its linearly interpolated Kaplan--Meier curve admits the uniform decomposition
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\varphi_{p,m,j}+b_{p,m,k}+q_{p,m,k}
 \quad\hbox{in }\ell^\infty(\mathcal I),
\]
where the \(\varphi_{p,m,j}\) are independent, mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes, \(\|b_{p,m,k}\|_\infty\le C_0e^{-c_0k}\), \(E q_{p,m,k}=0\), and \(E\|q_{p,m,k}\|_\infty^2\le C_0k^{-2}\), uniformly over the model class.  Here \(c_0=s_-g_-/3\), and \(C_0\) may be chosen as the conservative fixed constant used in the definition of \(\eta_D\).  For independent donor cells, averaging the \(q_{p,m,k}\) terms therefore has order \(O_P(N_0^{-1/2}k^{-1})=o_P((N_0k)^{-1/2})\), whereas averaging their bias terms need not improve the bound \(C_0e^{-c_0k}\).

For an observed control cell with \(k\) patients and \(k\) large enough, let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be the deterministic piecewise-linear interpolation operator on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and set \(\widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m}\).  Its linearly interpolated Kaplan--Meier curve admits the uniform decomposition
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}-\widetilde S^0_{p,m}
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\varphi_{p,m,j}+b_{p,m,k}+q_{p,m,k}
 \quad\hbox{in }\ell^\infty(\mathcal I),
\]
where the \(\varphi_{p,m,j}\) are independent, mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes, \(\|b_{p,m,k}\|_\infty\le C_0e^{-c_0k}\), \(E q_{p,m,k}=0\), and \(E\|q_{p,m,k}\|_\infty^2\le C_0k^{-2}\), uniformly over the model class.  Here \(c_0=s_-g_-/3\), and \(C_0\) may be chosen as the conservative fixed constant used in the definition of \(\eta_D\).  Moreover, with \(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\),
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}(g)=S^0_{p,m}(g)\quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}),
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_\infty
 \le c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_{L^2(\mathcal I)}
 \le \bar\tau^{1/2}c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
where \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)<\infty\).  Thus the exact expansion about \(S^0_{p,m}\) contains the additional deterministic term \(a_{\mathcal G,p,m}=\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\), which is zero on the grid and is controlled only by the displayed interpolation bounds.  For independent donor cells, averaging the \(q_{p,m,k}\) terms has order \(O_P(N_0^{-1/2}k^{-1})=o_P((N_0k)^{-1/2})\), whereas averaging the bias or interpolation terms need not improve their respective uniform bounds.
changed.reason: The frozen claim expands the linearly interpolated Kaplan--Meier curve directly about the un-interpolated population survival curve while bounding its entire deterministic term by an exponentially small risk-exhaustion bias. Linear interpolation contributes a generally nonzero off-grid deterministic remainder of order h^{q_beta}. The corrected claim recenters the stochastic expansion at the interpolated population curve, proves exact equality on the grid, and carries the population interpolation error separately in supremum and L2 norms.

For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices.  If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[

 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define the measurable positive-part scales \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\).  Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\).  Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\). \[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
The fitted curve is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace.  If a fold is empty, a selected eigenvalue is nonpositive, there is a cutoff tie, or \(\widehat H_0\) is singular, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve.  Thus \((\widehat s_p,\widehat b_p,\widehat z_\star,\widehat\theta_r)\) is a measurable function of every dataset.

On the regular event, differentiate the rotation-invariant composite map, including the spectral projector and positive square-root scales, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment. \]

\[

\[

 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\). Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\). \[
 \widehat\lambda_d\ge\gamma_-^2/4,

 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_0)\ge\kappa_-/4,

 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad

\]

On the regular event, differentiate this rotation-invariant interpolated-input map, including the selected spectral projector and positive square-root, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment. Let \(\widetilde\theta_r\) be the pointwise projection of \(\widehat\theta_r\) onto \([0,1]\), with value one imposed at zero. With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)\) from \(\mathrm{prop:grid\mbox{-}interpolation}\), and
\[

     +\omega_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
     +c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q},

define the grid endpoints by
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(g)=\max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r(g)-A_r\},
 \qquad

{"id":"lem:kaplan-meier-risk-exhaustion","kind":"lemma","statement":"For an observed control cell with \(k\) patients and \(k\) large enough, let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be the deterministic piecewise-linear interpolation operator on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and set \(\widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m}\).  Its linearly interpolated Kaplan--Meier curve admits the uniform decomposition
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}-\widetilde S^0_{p,m}
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\varphi_{p,m,j}+b_{p,m,k}+q_{p,m,k}
 \quad\hbox{in }\ell^\infty(\mathcal I),
\]
where the \(\varphi_{p,m,j}\) are independent, mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes, \(\|b_{p,m,k}\|_\infty\le C_0e^{-c_0k}\), \(E q_{p,m,k}=0\), and \(E\|q_{p,m,k}\|_\infty^2\le C_0k^{-2}\), uniformly over the model class.  Here \(c_0=s_-g_-/3\), and \(C_0\) may be chosen as the conservative fixed constant used in the definition of \(\eta_D\).  Moreover, with \(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\),
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}(g)=S^0_{p,m}(g)\quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}),
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_\infty
 \le c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_{L^2(\mathcal I)}
 \le \bar\tau^{1/2}c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
where \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)<\infty\).  Thus the exact expansion about \(S^0_{p,m}\) contains the additional deterministic term \(a_{\mathcal G,p,m}=\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\), which is zero on the grid and is controlled only by the displayed interpolation bounds.  For independent donor cells, averaging the \(q_{p,m,k}\) terms has order \(O_P(N_0^{-1/2}k^{-1})=o_P((N_0k)^{-1/2})\), whereas averaging the bias or interpolation terms need not improve their respective uniform bounds.","free_symbols":["KM","S","p","m","I","Kpm","N0","D","etaD"],"depends_on":["ass:patient-independence","ass:independent-censoring","ass:censor-overlap","ass:event-overlap","ass:hazard-smoothness","def:exact-rank-class","def:fpcr-multiplier-band"],"status":"to-prove"}

changed.from:
{"id":"def:fpcr-multiplier-band","name":"Censoring-aware functional-PCR martingale-multiplier band","construction":"Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}:C(\mathcal I)\to C(\mathcal I)\) be the deterministic piecewise-linear interpolation operator on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\). For a population panel set
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m},
 \qquad
 \widetilde s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde S^0_{p,m},
 \qquad
 \widetilde Y_m=(\widetilde S^0_{0,m}-\widetilde s_0,
                         \widetilde S^0_{1,m}-\widetilde s_1),
\]
and \(\widetilde\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde Y_m\otimes\widetilde Y_m\). Apply the same selected positive-square-root factor map and pre-period least-squares map described below to \((\widetilde S^0_{p,m})\), with the same fallback rule, and denote the resulting total population comparison curve by \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}\). For \(r=1\), set \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\widetilde s_1\). This comparison curve is a proof object defined through the interpolated \(L^2\) factor map; it is not a data-dependent estimator and it does not redefine the causal target \(\theta\).

On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\). For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices. If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, interpolate them by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\), center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\). Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\). Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\). On the regular event that both folds are nonempty,
\[
 \widehat\lambda_d\ge\gamma_-^2/4,
 \qquad
 \widehat\lambda_d-\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\ge\gamma_-^2/4,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_0)\ge\kappa_-/4,
\]
define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
Equivalently, this fitted curve is the coordinate-free selected-square-root map from the interpolated empirical panel to the post-period prediction; it is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace. If a fold is empty or any displayed threshold fails, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve. Thus \((\widehat s_p,\widehat b_p,\widehat z_\star,\widehat\theta_r)\) and all derivatives used below are uniformly bounded measurable functions of every dataset.

On the regular event, differentiate this rotation-invariant interpolated-input map, including the selected spectral projector and positive square-root, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment. On the fallback event, define the empirical derivative to be the ordinary pooled Kaplan--Meier derivative. Replace each patient contribution by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times that contribution, and let \(c_r^\xi\) be the conditional \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\)-quantile of its grid supremum, where
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}{2}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widetilde\theta_r\) be the pointwise projection of \(\widehat\theta_r\) onto \([0,1]\), with value one imposed at zero. With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)\) from \(\mathrm{prop:grid\mbox{-}interpolation}\), and
\[
 A_r=c_r^\xi+\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)
     +\omega_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
     +c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q},
\]
define the grid endpoints by
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(g)=\max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r(g)-A_r\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+A_r\}.
\]
Interpolate both endpoints linearly and impose the common value one at zero. This total measurable construction defines \(\widehat B_r\) and its multiplier process for every dataset. The allowance \(\eta_D\) is the exact deterministic half-fold risk-exhaustion envelope, \(\omega_r\) is the finite-tail nonlinear-remainder and multiplier-transfer buffer, and the discrepancy between \(S^0\) and \(\widetilde S^0\) away from the grid enters only through the final interpolation term in \(A_r\).","free_symbols":["KM","grid","N0","KT","KD","d","r","z","star","s","b","shat","bhat","zhat","thetahat","xi","p","m","M","D","j","O","alpha","epscov","Bhat","h","beta","L","taubar","I"],"inputs":["O","r","grid","xi","alpha","epscov"]}

changed.from: For fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and every fixed exact rank \(r\), there is \(a_0<\infty\) such that uniformly over every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), without relative-growth restrictions, \[W_1^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp(N_0K_D)^{-1/2},\qquad W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\quad(r\ge2).\] Here each infimum is over bands satisfying the coverage constraint at that same evaluated triple.
changed.to:
For fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and every fixed exact rank \(r\), there are \(a_0<\infty\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, uniformly over every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), without relative-growth restrictions,
\[
 W_1^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp(N_0K_D)^{-1/2},
\]
and, for \(r\ge2\),
\[
 c\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)
 \le W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 \le C\bar\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).
\]
Consequently \(W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) on every subregime satisfying \(\eta_D(K_D)=O(\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D))\).  Without that subregime condition, the displayed bracket is the proved unrestricted conclusion and its tightness is not asserted.  Each infimum is over bands satisfying the coverage constraint at that same evaluated triple.
changed.reason: The converse gives the lower rate \(\rho_r\), whereas the proved total functional-PCR band has the unrestricted upper envelope \(\bar\rho_r=\rho_r+\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)\). Because \(N_0\) and \(K_T\) may grow arbitrarily fast relative to \(K_D\), the exponential term \(\eta_D(K_D)\) need not be \(O(\rho_r)\) on the whole three-dimensional tail. The unrestricted higher-rank equivalence is therefore stronger than the declared proof basis; the proposed statement records the proved bracket and its matching subregime without changing the model class.

directive: Retain this OEQ as a distinct follow-on target, but replace the informal singular-value switch with the source-grounded CKLN Definition 2.2 / Theorems 2.1-2.2 / Section 7.1 program. Introduce a nested triangular closure P_1 subset P_{<=2}^{triangle} containing normalization-preserving rank-two laws approaching rank one. Thus the lower bound does not contradict their Theorem~2, and the functional-PCR upper bound over \(\mathfrak P_2\) does not transfer to this larger weak-pre-Gram class.

changed.from: Set \(s_p(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t)\). Write the singular-value decomposition of the primitive centered operator as \(\mathcal C_D=\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k u_k\otimes v_k\), ordered by decreasing \(\sigma_k\) with deterministic sign and tie-breaking rules. Define \(z_{m,k}=\sqrt{N_0}v_{k,m}\) and \(b_{p,k}(t)=\sigma_k u_{k,p}(t)\), so \(N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d\). Define the shared target coordinate \(z_\star\) by the unique coefficient equation \(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0=b_0^\top z_\star\). Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m\), \(s_p(0)=1\), and \(b_p(0)=0\). When \(d=0\), all vectors, sums, and Gram matrices in this construction are zero-dimensional.
changed.to:
Set
\[
 s_p(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t).
\]
Start from the model's target-compatible all-unit affine representation, center its donor loadings, covariance-normalize those loadings, and apply the inverse normalization to the factor curves. Write the singular-value decomposition of the resulting primitive centered operator as
\[
 \mathcal C_D=\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k u_k\otimes v_k,
\]
ordered by decreasing \(\sigma_k\) with deterministic sign and tie-breaking rules, and define
\[
 z_{m,k}=\sqrt{N_0}v_{k,m},
 \qquad b_{p,k}(t)=\sigma_k u_{k,p}(t).
\]
Thus the construction uses the donor-centered normalization
\[
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_m=0,
 \qquad N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d.
\]
Let
\[
 H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)b_0(t)^\top\,dt.
\]
Conditional on the model's target-pre factor compatibility
\(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0\in\operatorname{span}\{b_{0,1},\ldots,b_{0,d}\}\), define the shared target coordinate by
\[
 z_\star=H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)
 \{S^0_{0,\star}(t)-s_0(t)\}\,dt.
\]
The positive canonical pre-period Gram makes this coordinate unique. Transporting the compatible all-unit representation through the same covariance normalization and orthogonal donor-SVD transform gives
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m
\]
for both periods and every donor or target unit. Survival normalization gives \(s_p(0)=1\) and \(b_p(0)=0\). When \(d=0\), compatibility forces every contrast to vanish and all vectors, sums, and Gram matrices use the zero-dimensional convention.
changed.reason: The donor-operator singular-value decomposition alone does not establish target-pre span membership. The corrected construction begins with the model's compatible all-unit factorization, covariance-normalizes its full-rank donor loadings, transports the compatible target coordinate, and uses the positive canonical pre-period Gram only for uniqueness.

changed.from: Choose a deterministic grid \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\) containing \(0\) and \(\bar\tau\) whose mesh satisfies \(h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}\le\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), and use piecewise-linear interpolation between adjacent grid points.
changed.to:
Put \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\) and
\[
 J_r=\max\left\{1,
 \left\lceil\bar\tau\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)^{-1/q}\right\rceil
 \right\}.
\]
Define the canonical quasi-uniform grid and its adjacent-knot mesh by
\[
 \mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}
 =\left\{\frac{\ell\bar\tau}{J_r}:0\le\ell\le J_r\right\},
 \qquad h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=\frac{\bar\tau}{J_r}.
\]
Use piecewise-linear interpolation between adjacent knots. Then
\[
 h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\le\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D),
 \qquad
 |\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}|
 \le2+\bar\tau\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)^{-1/q}.
\]
changed.reason: The mesh symbol must denote adjacent-knot spacing, and the multiplier and interpolation arguments need an explicit measurable quasi-uniform grid with a cardinality bound. The corrected construction supplies both from the same rate-matched integer \(J_r\).

changed.from:
Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}:C(\mathcal I)\to C(\mathcal I)\) be the deterministic piecewise-linear interpolation operator on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\). For a population panel set
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m},
 \qquad
 \widetilde s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde S^0_{p,m},
 \qquad
 \widetilde Y_m=(\widetilde S^0_{0,m}-\widetilde s_0,
                         \widetilde S^0_{1,m}-\widetilde s_1),
\]
and \(\widetilde\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde Y_m\otimes\widetilde Y_m\). Apply the same selected positive-square-root factor map and pre-period least-squares map described below to \((\widetilde S^0_{p,m})\), with the same fallback rule, and denote the resulting total population comparison curve by \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}\). For \(r=1\), set \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\widetilde s_1\). This comparison curve is a proof object defined through the interpolated \(L^2\) factor map; it is not a data-dependent estimator and it does not redefine the causal target \(\theta\).

On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\). For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices. If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, interpolate them by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\), center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\). Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\). Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\). On the regular event that both folds are nonempty,
\[
 \widehat\lambda_d\ge\gamma_-^2/4,
 \qquad
 \widehat\lambda_d-\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\ge\gamma_-^2/4,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_0)\ge\kappa_-/4,
\]
define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
Equivalently, this fitted curve is the coordinate-free selected-square-root map from the interpolated empirical panel to the post-period prediction; it is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace. If a fold is empty or any displayed threshold fails, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve. Thus \((\widehat s_p,\widehat b_p,\widehat z_\star,\widehat\theta_r)\) and all derivatives used below are uniformly bounded measurable functions of every dataset.

On the regular event, differentiate this rotation-invariant interpolated-input map, including the selected spectral projector and positive square-root, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment. On the fallback event, define the empirical derivative to be the ordinary pooled Kaplan--Meier derivative. Replace each patient contribution by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times that contribution, and let \(c_r^\xi\) be the conditional \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\)-quantile of its grid supremum, where
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}{2}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widetilde\theta_r\) be the pointwise projection of \(\widehat\theta_r\) onto \([0,1]\), with value one imposed at zero. With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)\) from \(\mathrm{prop:grid\mbox{-}interpolation}\), and
\[
 A_r=c_r^\xi+\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)
     +\omega_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
     +c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q},
\]
define the grid endpoints by
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(g)=\max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r(g)-A_r\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+A_r\}.
\]
Interpolate both endpoints linearly and impose the common value one at zero. This total measurable construction defines \(\widehat B_r\) and its multiplier process for every dataset. The allowance \(\eta_D\) is the exact deterministic half-fold risk-exhaustion envelope, \(\omega_r\) is the finite-tail nonlinear-remainder and multiplier-transfer buffer, and the discrepancy between \(S^0\) and \(\widetilde S^0\) away from the grid enters only through the final interpolation term in \(A_r\).
changed.to:
Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on the canonical grid. For the population comparison, define
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m},\qquad
 \widetilde s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde S^0_{p,m},
\]
\[
 \widetilde Y_m=(\widetilde S^0_{0,m}-\widetilde s_0,
                  \widetilde S^0_{1,m}-\widetilde s_1),\qquad
 \widetilde\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \widetilde Y_m\otimes\widetilde Y_m.
\]
Apply the selected positive-square-root and pre-period least-squares prediction map below to this panel and call the result \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}\); for \(r=1\), put \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\widetilde s_1\). This is a proof comparison and does not redefine \(\theta\).

Put \(h_0=s_-g_-\). For any cell or deterministic half-fold containing \(k\) patients, set
\[
 \ell_k=\max\{1,kh_0/8\},\qquad
 Y_k^\dagger(u)=\max\{Y_k(u),\ell_k\}.
\]
Order tied observed failures lexicographically by failure time and patient index, updating the risk count after each ordered failure, and define
\[
 \widehat S_k^\dagger(t)=
 \prod_{u\le t}\left\{1-\frac{dN_k(u)}{Y_k^\dagger(u)}\right\}.
\]
Every ordered increment is zero or one, so this measurable curve lies in \([0,1]\) on every dataset. Interpolate it by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\). For every \(r\ge2\), use these stabilized curves for the target-pre full cell, every donor full cell, and both odd--even donor half-folds. For \(r=1\), do not stabilize: pool all \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records first, form the ordinary aggregate-risk product-limit curve with its empty-risk convention, and interpolate it continuously.

For \(r\ge2\), center the two sets of stabilized half-fold donor curves across donors to obtain \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\), and form
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
   \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\}.
\]
Select its largest \(d\) eigenvalues with deterministic lexicographic basis and sign rules, put \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\), and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}\). Let \(\widehat s_p\) be the donor average of the stabilized full-cell curves, and let \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0\widehat b_0^\top\). On the aggregate regular event
\[
 \widehat\lambda_d\ge\gamma_-^2/4,\qquad
 \widehat\lambda_d-\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\ge\gamma_-^2/4,
 \qquad \lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_0)\ge\kappa_-/4,
\]
define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S_{0,\star}^\dagger(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
This is the rotation-invariant selected-projector, positive-square-root, and inverse-pre-Gram prediction map. If a fold is empty or an aggregate threshold fails, set the factor and loading estimates to zero and let \(\widehat\theta_r\) be the continuously interpolated ordinary pooled donor-post product-limit curve. Thus every branch is total, measurable, and continuous.

On the regular branch, differentiate the coordinate-free prediction map and the stabilized product-limit inputs. The observed contribution of patient \(j\) in a stabilized \(k\)-patient input uses the weight
\[
 -\widehat S_k^\dagger(t-)
 \int_0^t\{Y_k^\dagger(u)\}^{-1}\,dN_{k,j}(u).
\]
On the fallback and rank-one branches use the ordinary pooled aggregate-risk derivative. Attach independent standard Gaussian multipliers to the patient contributions and denote the resulting interpolated process by \(\widehat Z_r^\xi\). Define its conditional covariance by
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_r(g,g')
 =E_\xi\{\widehat Z_r^\xi(g)\widehat Z_r^\xi(g')\mid O\}.
\]
Put
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac\alpha2,
 \frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}2\right\},
\]
and define the left-continuous generalized-inverse conditional quantile by
\[
 \widetilde c_r^\xi=
 \inf\left\{x\ge0:
 P_\xi\left(\max_{g\in\mathcal G}|\widehat Z_r^\xi(g)|\le x
 \mid O\right)\ge q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\right\}.
\]
For the explicit deterministic constants set
\[
 C_\partial=2^{12}r^2(1+\bar\tau)^2
 (1+M_b+M_z+M_\star+\gamma_+)^2
 (1+\gamma_-^{-1}+\kappa_-^{-1})^4,
\]
\[
 C_Z=2^{12}(1+L\bar\tau)^2(s_-g_-)^{-2}(1+C_\partial)^2.
\]
Put
\[
 d_r(\alpha)=\left(\frac{2C_Z}{\alpha}\right)^{1/2}\rho_r,
 \qquad c_r^\xi=\max\{\widetilde c_r^\xi,d_r(\alpha)\}.
\]
Thus \(c_r^\xi\) is a guarded multiplier critical radius; coverage is certified by the deterministic guard rather than by a multiplier-only random-quantile theorem.

Project \(\widehat\theta_r\) pointwise onto \([0,1]\), impose value one at zero, and call the result \(\widetilde\theta_r\). With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), define
\[
 A_r=c_r^\xi+\mathbf1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)
 +\omega_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 +c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}.
\]
At each grid knot set
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}=
 \max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r-A_r\},\qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}=
 \min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r+A_r\},
\]
interpolate both endpoints linearly between adjacent knots, and impose their common value one at zero. This defines the guarded martingale-multiplier functional-PCR band on every dataset.
changed.reason: Ordinary cellwise product-limit derivatives are not globally bounded on exhausted-risk datasets, and the prior multiplier-only quantile route was not justified. The corrected construction uses observable stabilized higher-rank inputs, preserves the ordinary pooled rank-one branch, makes every fallback total, and guards the multiplier radius by a deterministic patient-martingale moment bound.

{"id":"lem:gridwise-fpcr-multiplier-transfer","kind":"lemma","statement":"Put \(n_D=N_0K_D\), and use the canonical grid and corrected multiplier construction. On the regular spectral and pre-Gram event, the rotation-invariant functional-PCR prediction map from the interpolated cellwise product-limit inputs to \(\mathbb R^{|\mathcal G|}\) is twice Fr\'echet differentiable, with first and second derivative envelopes bounded uniformly over the exact-rank class. Its individual target-pre and donor-patient derivative weights are bounded respectively by \(C/K_T\) and \(C/n_D\). The complement of the regular event is uniformly negligible at the nonlinear-remainder scale. Consequently, for every fixed \(r\ge2\), the empirical functional-PCR estimator has a gridwise expansion
\[
 \widehat\theta_r-\theta=Z_r+\mathfrak b_r+Q_r,
 \qquad
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}\le\eta_D(K_D),
\]
with the two independent patient channels displayed in \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}linearization}\), and
\[
 \sup_PE_P\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}^2\le Cv_r^2,
 \qquad
 \sup_PE_PE_\xi\|\widehat Z_r^\xi\|_{infty,\mathcal G}^2\le C\rho_r^2,
\]
where \(v_r\) is the deterministic quantity in the definition of \(\omega_r\). If \(c_r^\xi\) is the conditional quantile in the band definition and \(\chi_r\) is the corresponding comparison quantity in the definition of \(\omega_r\), then
\[
 \sup_PP\{\|Z_r\|_{infty,\mathcal G}>c_r^\xi+x\}
 \le1-q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}+C\{\chi_r/x+v_r^2/x^2\},
 \qquad x>0.
\]
In particular, for sufficiently large triples and sufficiently large fixed \(C_\omega\), the two finite-tail inequalities asserted in \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}linearization}\) hold and \(\omega_r=o(\rho_r)\) uniformly on every three-dimensional tail. No positive lower variance or anti-concentration condition is required.","free_symbols":["r","N0","KT","KD","grid","Pr","P","thetahat","theta","rho","etaD","omega","xi","alpha","epscov","I"],"depends_on":["ass:control-consistency","ass:patient-independence","ass:independent-censoring","ass:censor-overlap","ass:event-overlap","ass:hazard-smoothness","ass:normalized-factor-model","ass:exact-centered-rank","ass:centered-contrast-spectrum","ass:pre-contrast-gram","ass:donor-incoherence","ass:target-loading-bound","ass:factor-envelope","def:exact-rank-class","def:inference-grid","def:fpcr-multiplier-band","lem:canonical-target-coordinate","lem:kaplan-meier-risk-exhaustion","lem:interpolated-population-fpcr-stability"],"status":"to-prove","justification":"This provides the finite-grid derivative, covariance, entropy, fallback, and random-quantile theorem required by the feasible band.","gap":"Spectral and Gram stability in an internal L2 norm does not by itself justify a grid-uniform multiplier for a data-dependent nonlinear predictor.","consumer":"It turns the product-limit first stages into a uniformly honest functional-PCR critical value without a variance lower bound."}

{"id":"def:canonical-factorization","name":"Canonical normalized survival-factor coordinates","construction":"Set
\[
 s_p(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t).
\]
Start from the model's target-compatible all-unit affine representation, center its donor loadings, covariance-normalize those loadings, and apply the inverse normalization to the factor curves. Write the singular-value decomposition of the resulting primitive centered operator as
\[
 \mathcal C_D=\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k u_k\otimes v_k,
\]
ordered by decreasing \(\sigma_k\) with deterministic sign and tie-breaking rules, and define
\[
 z_{m,k}=\sqrt{N_0}v_{k,m},
 \qquad b_{p,k}(t)=\sigma_k u_{k,p}(t).
\]
Thus the construction uses the donor-centered normalization
\[
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_m=0,
 \qquad N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d.
\]
Let
\[
 H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)b_0(t)^\top\,dt.
\]
Conditional on the model's target-pre factor compatibility
\(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0\in\operatorname{span}\{b_{0,1},\ldots,b_{0,d}\}\), define the shared target coordinate by
\[
 z_\star=H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)
 \{S^0_{0,\star}(t)-s_0(t)\}\,dt.
\]
The positive canonical pre-period Gram makes this coordinate unique. Transporting the compatible all-unit representation through the same covariance normalization and orthogonal donor-SVD transform gives
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m
\]
for both periods and every donor or target unit. Survival normalization gives \(s_p(0)=1\) and \(b_p(0)=0\). {"id":"def:fpcr-multiplier-band","name":"Censoring-aware functional-PCR martingale-multiplier band","construction":"Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on the canonical grid. For the population comparison, define
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m},\qquad
 \widetilde s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde S^0_{p,m},
\]
\[
 \widetilde Y_m=(\widetilde S^0_{0,m}-\widetilde s_0,
                  \widetilde S^0_{1,m}-\widetilde s_1),\qquad
 \widetilde\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \widetilde Y_m\otimes\widetilde Y_m.
\]
Apply the selected positive-square-root and pre-period least-squares prediction map below to this panel and call the result \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}\); for \(r=1\), put \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\widetilde s_1\). This is a proof comparison and does not redefine \(\theta\).

Put \(h_0=s_-g_-\). For any cell or deterministic half-fold containing \(k\) patients, set
\[
 \ell_k=\max\{1,kh_0/8\},\qquad
 Y_k^\dagger(u)=\max\{Y_k(u),\ell_k\}.
\]
Order tied observed failures lexicographically by failure time and patient index, updating the risk count after each ordered failure, and define
\[
 \widehat S_k^\dagger(t)=
 \prod_{u\le t}\left\{1-\frac{dN_k(u)}{Y_k^\dagger(u)}\right\}.
\]
Every ordered increment is zero or one, so this measurable curve lies in \([0,1]\) on every dataset. Interpolate it by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\). For every \(r\ge2\), use these stabilized curves for the target-pre full cell, every donor full cell, and both odd--even donor half-folds. For \(r=1\), do not stabilize: pool all \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records first, form the ordinary aggregate-risk product-limit curve with its empty-risk convention, and interpolate it continuously.

For \(r\ge2\), center the two sets of stabilized half-fold donor curves across donors to obtain \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\), and form
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
   \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\}.
\]
Select its largest \(d\) eigenvalues with deterministic lexicographic basis and sign rules, put \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\), and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}\). Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on the canonical grid. For the population comparison, define
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m},\qquad
 \widetilde s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde S^0_{p,m},
\]
\[
 \widetilde Y_m=(\widetilde S^0_{0,m}-\widetilde s_0,
                  \widetilde S^0_{1,m}-\widetilde s_1),\qquad
 \widetilde\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \widetilde Y_m\otimes\widetilde Y_m.
\]
Apply the selected positive-square-root and pre-period least-squares prediction map below to this panel and call the result \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}\); for \(r=1\), put \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\widetilde s_1\). This is a proof comparison and does not redefine \(\theta\).

Put \(h_0=s_-g_-\). For any cell or deterministic half-fold containing \(k\) patients, set
\[
 \ell_k=\max\{1,kh_0/8\},\qquad
 Y_k^\dagger(u)=\max\{Y_k(u),\ell_k\}.
\]
Order tied observed failures lexicographically by failure time and patient index, updating the risk count after each ordered failure, and define
\[
 \widehat S_k^\dagger(t)=
 \prod_{u\le t}\left\{1-\frac{dN_k(u)}{Y_k^\dagger(u)}\right\}.
\]
Every ordered increment is zero or one, so this measurable curve lies in \([0,1]\) on every dataset. Interpolate it by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\). For every \(r\ge2\), use these stabilized curves for the target-pre full cell, every donor full cell, and both odd--even donor half-folds. For \(r=1\), do not stabilize: pool all \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records first, form the ordinary aggregate-risk product-limit curve with its empty-risk convention, and interpolate it continuously.

For \(r\ge2\), center the two sets of stabilized half-fold donor curves across donors to obtain \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\), and form
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
   \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\}.
\]
Select its largest \(d\) eigenvalues with deterministic lexicographic basis and sign rules, put \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\), and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}\). Let \(\widehat s_p\) be the donor average of the stabilized full-cell curves, and let \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0\widehat b_0^\top\). On the aggregate regular event
\[
 \widehat\lambda_d\ge\gamma_-^2/4,\qquad
 \widehat\lambda_d-\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\ge\gamma_-^2/4,
 \qquad \lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_0)\ge\kappa_-/4,
\]
define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S_{0,\star}^\dagger(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
This is the rotation-invariant selected-projector, positive-square-root, and inverse-pre-Gram prediction map. If a fold is empty or an aggregate threshold fails, set the factor and loading estimates to zero and let \(\widehat\theta_r\) be the continuously interpolated ordinary pooled donor-post product-limit curve. Thus every branch is total, measurable, and continuous.

On the regular branch, differentiate the coordinate-free prediction map and the stabilized product-limit inputs. The observed contribution of patient \(j\) in a stabilized \(k\)-patient input uses the weight
\[
 -\widehat S_k^\dagger(t-)
 \int_0^t\{Y_k^\dagger(u)\}^{-1}\,dN_{k,j}(u).
\]
On the fallback and rank-one branches use the ordinary pooled aggregate-risk derivative. Attach independent standard Gaussian multipliers to the patient contributions and denote the resulting interpolated process by \(\widehat Z_r^\xi\). Define its conditional covariance by
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_r(g,g')
 =E_\xi\{\widehat Z_r^\xi(g)\widehat Z_r^\xi(g')\mid O\}.
\]
Put
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac\alpha2,
 \frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}2\right\},
\]
and define the left-continuous generalized-inverse conditional quantile by
\[
 \widetilde c_r^\xi=
 \inf\left\{x\ge0:
 P_\xi\left(\max_{g\in\mathcal G}|\widehat Z_r^\xi(g)|\le x
 \mid O\right)\ge q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\right\}.
\]
For the explicit deterministic constants set
\[
 C_\partial=2^{12}r^2(1+\bar\tau)^2
 (1+M_b+M_z+M_\star+\gamma_+)^2
 (1+\gamma_-^{-1}+\kappa_-^{-1})^4,
\]
\[
 C_Z=2^{12}(1+L\bar\tau)^2(s_-g_-)^{-2}(1+C_\partial)^2.
\]
Put
\[
 d_r(\alpha)=\left(\frac{2C_Z}{\alpha}\right)^{1/2}\rho_r,
 \qquad c_r^\xi=\max\{\widetilde c_r^\xi,d_r(\alpha)\}.
\]
Thus \(c_r^\xi\) is a guarded multiplier critical radius; coverage is certified by the deterministic guard rather than by a multiplier-only random-quantile theorem.

Project \(\widehat\theta_r\) pointwise onto \([0,1]\), impose value one at zero, and call the result \(\widetilde\theta_r\). With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), define
\[
 A_r=c_r^\xi+\mathbf1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)
 +\omega_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 +c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}.
\]
At each grid knot set
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}=
 \max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r-A_r\},\qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}=
 \min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r+A_r\},
\]
interpolate both endpoints linearly between adjacent knots, and impose their common value one at zero. This defines the guarded martingale-multiplier functional-PCR band on every dataset.

{"id":"lem:uniform-linearization","kind":"lemma","statement":"Put \(n_D=N_0K_D\), let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and center the functional-PCR map at the interpolated population panel \(\widetilde S^0=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and all sequences with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\to\infty\), there are independent mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes \(\phi_{T,j}\) and \(\phi_{D,p,m,j}\), a deterministic grid function \(\mathfrak b_r\), and a remainder \(Q_r\) such that, simultaneously for \(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)=Z_r(g)+\mathfrak b_r(g)+Q_r(g),
 \qquad
 Z_r=\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}K_T^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_T}\phi_{T,j}
     +n_D^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\phi_{D,p,m,j},
\]
where \(\phi_{T,j}\equiv0\) when \(r=1\) and
\[
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}
 \le \mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D).

\]
\[
 \widetilde Y_m=(\widetilde S^0_{0,m}-\widetilde s_0,

 \widetilde\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \widetilde Y_m\otimes\widetilde Y_m.
\]

\[

 Y_k^\dagger(u)=\max\{Y_k(u),\ell_k\}.
\]
Order tied observed failures lexicographically by failure time and patient index, updating the risk count after each ordered failure, and define
\[
 \widehat S_k^\dagger(t)=
 \prod_{u\le t}\left\{1-\frac{dN_k(u)}{Y_k^\dagger(u)}\right\}.
\]
Every ordered increment is zero or one, so this measurable curve lies in \([0,1]\) on every dataset. Interpolate it by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\). For every \(r\ge2\), use these stabilized curves for the target-pre full cell, every donor full cell, and both odd--even donor half-folds. For \(r=1\), do not stabilize: pool all \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records first, form the ordinary aggregate-risk product-limit curve with its empty-risk convention, and interpolate it continuously.

For \(r\ge2\), center the two sets of stabilized half-fold donor curves across donors to obtain \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\), and form
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
   \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\}.
\]
Select its largest \(d\) eigenvalues with deterministic lexicographic basis and sign rules, put \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\), and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}\). \[
 \widehat\lambda_d\ge\gamma_-^2/4,\qquad
 \widehat\lambda_d-\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\ge\gamma_-^2/4,
 \qquad \lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_0)\ge\kappa_-/4,
\]
define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S_{0,\star}^\dagger(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]

If a fold is empty or an aggregate threshold fails, set the factor and loading estimates to zero and let \(\widehat\theta_r\) be the continuously interpolated ordinary pooled donor-post product-limit curve. Thus every branch is total, measurable, and continuous.

On the regular branch, differentiate the coordinate-free prediction map and the stabilized product-limit inputs. The observed contribution of patient \(j\) in a stabilized \(k\)-patient input uses the weight
\[
 -\widehat S_k^\dagger(t-)
 \int_0^t\{Y_k^\dagger(u)\}^{-1}\,dN_{k,j}(u).
\]

\[
 \widehat\Sigma_r(g,g')
 =E_\xi\{\widehat Z_r^\xi(g)\widehat Z_r^\xi(g')\mid O\}.
\]

\[
 n_{\mathrm{eff},r}=
 \begin{cases}
 n_D,&r=1,\\
 \min\{K_T,n_D\},&r\ge2.
 \end{cases}

\[

 \left\{K_T^{-1/2}+K_D^{-1/2}+\eta_D(K_D)
 +e^{-c_0K_T/2}+e^{-c_0n_D/2}\right\}.
\]

\[
 k_{r,n}=\max\{2,\lceil n_{\mathrm{eff},r}^{1/9}\rceil\},
 \qquad p_{\mathrm c,r,n}=2(k_{r,n}+1),
\]

\[

 \qquad
 \zeta_{r,n}=U_{r,n}^{1/4}\{1+|\log U_{r,n}|\}.
\]

\[
 \chi_{r,n}=C_\chi\left[
 \zeta_{r,n}+a_{r,n}^{1/48}\{1+|\log a_{r,n}|\}\right],
 \qquad
 \tau_{r,n}=\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\chi_{r,n},
\]
and
\[
 \delta_{r,n}(\alpha)=
 \min\left\{\frac\alpha2,
 \frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}2\right\}.
\]
Set \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+\delta_{r,n}(\alpha)\), and define the left-continuous generalized-inverse conditional quantile by
\[

 \inf\left\{x\ge0:
 P_\xi\left(\max_{g\in\mathcal G}|\widehat Z_r^\xi(g)|\le x

Project \(\widehat\theta_r\) pointwise onto \([0,1]\), impose value one at zero, and call the result \(\widetilde\theta_r\). With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), define
\[
 A_r=\widetilde c_r^\xi+\tau_{r,n}
 +\mathbf1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)
 +\omega_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 +c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}.
\]
At each grid knot set
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}=
 \max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r-A_r\},\qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}=
 \min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r+A_r\},
\]
interpolate both endpoints linearly between adjacent knots, and impose their common value one at zero. \emph{Covariance and modulus derivation.}

\[

 Cn_D^{-1},&i\text{ is a donor patient}.
 \end{cases}                                                   \tag{A.1}
\]

We first compare covariance kernels. In rank one, the explicit formulas in the pooled product-limit calculation are
\[
 \Sigma_1(s,t)=\frac{s_1(s)s_1(t)}{n_D}
 \int_0^{s\wedge t}\frac{\lambda_1(u)}{H_D(u)}\,du,
\]
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_1(s,t)=\widehat S_D(s-)\widehat S_D(t-)
 \int_0^{s\wedge t}\frac{J_Y(u)}{Y(u)^2}\,dN(u).          \tag{A.2}
\]
On \(\{\inf_{u\le\bar\tau}Y(u)\ge n_Dh_0/2\}\), substitute \(dN=dM+Y\lambda_1du\) in (A.2). Predictable isometry, the maximal inequality, and the time-ordered empirical-risk bound give
\[
 E\sup_v\left|
 \int_0^v\frac{n_D}{Y(u)^2}\,dN(u)
 -\int_0^v\frac{\lambda_1(u)}{H_D(u)}\,du
 \right|\le Cn_D^{-1/2}.                                  \tag{A.3}
\]

\[
 E\{\rho_1^{-2}\|\widehat\Sigma_1-\Sigma_1\|_\infty\}
 \le Cn_D^{-1/2}=Ca_{1,n}.                                \tag{A.4}
\]

For a contour \(\mathscr C\) lying in the fixed spectral gap, the resolvent identity gives the explicit selected-projector perturbation
\[
 \widehat\Pi-\Pi
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\mathscr C}
 (z-\widehat\Gamma)^{-1}(\widehat\Gamma-\Gamma)
 (z-\Gamma)^{-1}\,dz.
\]
The positive-square-root derivative is the unique selected-range solution of
\[
 A\,DA_\Gamma[E]+DA_\Gamma[E]A
 =D(\Pi\Gamma\Pi)_\Gamma[E].
\]
The contour distance and the selected eigenvalue lower bound make both displayed derivative maps uniformly Lipschitz. With \(H=A_0^*A_0\), the inverse pre-Gram perturbation is controlled by
\[
 \widehat H^{-1}-H^{-1}
 =\widehat H^{-1}(H-\widehat H)H^{-1},
\]
and the two pre-Gram inverses are uniformly bounded by the fixed positive Gram thresholds. These three identities, differentiated once where necessary, imply
\[

 \le C\{K_T^{-1/2}+n_D^{-1/2}+\eta_D(K_D)\}              \tag{A.5}
\]
in mean, after truncation at the fixed spectral and pre-Gram thresholds. For a stabilized cell of size \(k\), write \(H_k=S^0G\), and define the naturally normalized oracle and empirical cell covariance kernels by
\[

 \frac{\lambda^0(u)}{H_k(u)}\,du,
\]
\[

 \widehat S_k^\dagger(t-)
 \int_0^{s\wedge t}\{Y_k^\dagger(u)\}^{-2}\,dN_k(u).

\[

\[

\]

\[

Let \(k=k_{r,n}\), and choose a deterministic subset \(\mathcal T_n\subset\mathcal G\) of at most \(k+1\) knots whose physical-time mesh is at most \(C/k\). \[

\]
We invoke Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014), Theorem~4.2, directly.  In the finite-dimensional form used here, if \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are independent centered vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\), \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N\) are independent centered Gaussian vectors with \(E(Y_iY_i^\top)=E(X_iX_i^\top)\), and \(a>0\), then, with
\[

\[

\[
 B_0\le C p_{\mathrm c,r,n}^{5/2}m^{-1/2}a^{-3}

\]

The interval-count, semimetric, and Bernstein bounds (A.9)--(A.13) transfer this coupling to the canonical grid. Indeed, with \(u=C/k\), its Bernstein bound gives
\[
 \max_{\substack{g,g'\in\mathcal G\\|g-g'|\le u}}

\]

1. Hard-branch stability root repair. Keep the present hard regular/fallback estimator, but correct all false global differentiability and all-dataset replacement wording. In the definition, distinguish the derivative of the regular FPCR branch and the derivative of the pooled fallback branch from a derivative of the total hard-switched map; the branchwise multiplier coefficients are explicitly defined coefficients, not a global derivative across the cutoff.

Define a strengthened regular-margin event M with fixed positive slack above the selected-eigenvalue, eigengap, and pre-Gram cutoffs and with the same regular branch for every one-donor-patient replacement. Use the deterministic O(1/(N0 KD)) perturbation of the aggregate donor covariance, eigenvalue/resolvent bounds, pre-Gram perturbation, and the fixed population slack to prove uniformly that P(M^c) <= C exp(-c N0 KD) eventually.
